title: Quotinator Per-Source Conflict-Resolution Rule File
description: A minimal, hand-authored set of rules (#181) that auto-resolve a field for a specific entity (Quote, Series, Universe, or any other type whose planner wires in ConflictRuleLookup) instead of leaving it staged Pending under the review duplicate-resolution policy. One rule file per bundled source, referenced from that source's own manifest.json entry via ruleFile. #153 (Phase 2) will later add a generated, declarative form of this same file shape.

rules.description: Every entity this file declares a rule for. Empty for a source with no known recurring conflicts. Grouped by entity (one entry per entity), not flattened to one entry per field — a single entity can have more than one field in conflict at once. An entity must be named at most once (ADR 023); JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by a property, so that half is enforced by SourceDataIntegrityTests.RuleFiles_NameEachEntityAtMostOnce rather than here. A single rules array can mix ids from more than one entity type (e.g. a Quote id alongside a Series id).

entityId.description: The entity's own id (matched case-insensitively, per this project's id-comparison convention).

existingRecord.description: The existing (already-seeded) side's complete field set, recorded at the time this rule was authored — lets a human reviewing this file see the whole record, not only the field(s) actually being resolved. Purely documentation, never read by the matching logic.

incomingRecord.description: The incoming (this source file's own) side's complete field set, recorded at the time this rule was authored — same shape and same human-review purpose as existingRecord. Purely documentation, never read by the matching logic: staleness is judged per field, against that field's own recordedIncomingValue (ADR 023). Before ADR 023 this record was what the matching logic read, which is why one entity could need two entries and no single snapshot was correct for every field.

fields.description: Every field of this entity that this rule file resolves. Not limited to fields that actually disagree between the two sides — a Custom rule can also correct a field that's simply wrong or missing on both.

field.description: The field name this rule governs (e.g. 'date', 'type', 'source', 'quoteText', 'character', 'author', 'originalLanguage', 'genres') — a key present in both existingRecord and incomingRecord.

recordedIncomingValue.description: This field's own incoming value, as it stood when this rule was authored — the value the matching logic compares against the live import's incoming value to detect a stale rule (the source moved since authoring) or a retirable one (the two sides have moved into agreement). Deliberately carries no type constraint: a recorded value is legitimately a string, null, or an array (genres), and null is a real recorded value rather than an absence. Recorded per field, not per entry, so one entity never needs two entries to carry two snapshots — see ADR 023. Required here, but a hand-written file that omits it degrades to Stale rather than silently reapplying.

resolution.description: Keep — resolve to the existing (already-seeded) side's value. Replace — resolve to the incoming (this file's own) value. Custom — resolve to customValue, a value neither side actually has (e.g. correcting a field that's missing from both, not just disagreed upon).

customValue.description: The value to use when resolution is Custom. Required when resolution is Custom; must be omitted otherwise.
